sources.citation: Vogt, Friedrich. 1904. Die Indianer des Obern Paraná. Mitteilungen der Anthropologischen Gesellschaft in Wien 34: 200–221, 353–377.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Primary Ingain wordlists (sister variety; same language per Nikulin 2020) with the diacritics Jolkesky analyses; any remark by Vogt on 'Betonung' would be the closest thing to a first-hand accent statement for Ingain-Kimdá.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record kimd1235 and reference record 161059 (hh:w:Lista:Misiones), incl. Hammarström langnote on the two Kimdá sources.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliographic only: Glottolog's fullest description is only a wordlist (Lista 1883, 124 pp.); no grammar, sketch or phonology listed.

sources.citation: Nikulin, Andrey. 2020. Proto-Macro-Jê: um estudo reconstrutivo. Tese de doutorado, Universidade de Brasília.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: §1.1.1.4 p.16: Ingain† (Kimdá†) [inga1253] material 'extremamente limitado tanto em quantidade como em qualidade.. pequenas listas de palavras transcritas de forma não uniformizada' (Lista 1883, Ambrosetti 1896, Vogt 1904); Ingain and Kimdá treated as one language. No statement on Ingain/Kimdá stress anywhere in the thesis (a full-text search for stress/accent acento/tônic/oxíton).

sources.citation: Jolkesky, Marcelo Pinho de Valhery. 2010. Reconstrução fonológica e lexical do Proto-Jê Meridional. Dissertação de mestrado, Universidade Estadual de Campinas (IEL). PDF 349 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Kimdá explicitly excluded from phonological analysis (p.1 'Objetivo'; §1.5 p.18): only 56 (Patiño 1863) + 11 (Lista 1883) items exist, 'o que praticamente impede sua sistematização e análise fonológica'. §4.5.1.2.1 'Acentuação' (pp.131–134) treats the acute accent in the INGAIN corpora (Ambrosetti 1896, Vogt 1904) as ambiguous between stress and vowel quality; Vogt's accent suppression on first members of compounds suggests 'a palavra fonológica nesta língua apresente um padrão acentual oxítono (como também é o caso em Xokleng e Kaingang)'; Ingain tonic syllables assumed to pattern like Kaing…

sources.citation: D'Angelis, Wilmar da Rocha. 2003. O primeiro século de registro da língua Kaingang (1842-1950): valor e uso da documentação etnográfica. Campinas/Portal Kaingang, 39 pp. (§2.10 Ambrosetti 1896 [Ingain]; §3.4 Martinez 1904 [Guayanã vocabularies of Patiño and Lista]; §3.5 Vogt 1904).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No remarks on accent notation or stress in the Ingain/Guayanã sources; content is bibliographic/lexical (syllable loss in Ingain 'Ñara/Ñere' vs Kaingang kajẽre, Borba 1908's scepticism, Martínez's own notation of 6 words).

sources.citation: Susnik, Branislava & Miguel Chase-Sardi. 1995. Los indios del Paraguay. Madrid: Editorial MAPFRE (Colecciones MAPFRE 1492). pp. 225–226 on the guaraní-guayaná village of Pirapytay/Villa Azara (citing Patiño, Diario, 7, 14, 15); index 'Gualacho-guayaná', 'Guayaná-gé'.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: no phonology content (historical/ethnographic narrative only); confirms Susnik used Patiño's Diario directly (page refs 7, 14, 15), a lead for locating the 1864/1881 print.

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1968. Classification of South American Indian languages. Los Angeles: UCLA Latin American Center. 'Kaingán stock — Southern languages: Guayana or Wayana or Gualachí or Guanhanan.. [Borba 1908, pp. 138-139; Ihering 1904; Lista 1883, pp. 112-113; B. Martínez 1901, 1904, 1919]; Ingain or Tain [Ambrosetti 1896]; Amhó or Ivitorocái [Vogt 1904, pp. 360-376]' + comparative table Guayana/Ingain/Amhó.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Classification entry and an 11-item word table only; no phonology. Useful for its source pointers (Borba 1908; B. Martínez 1901, 1904, 1919).

sources.citation: Portnoy, Antonio. 1936. Estado actual del estudio de las lenguas indígenas que se hablaron en el territorio argentino. Buenos Aires: Instituto de Filología, Universidad de Buenos Aires. (archive.org item 'Estudio de las lenguas indígenas, Buenos Aires 1936'; national survey with one chapter per language/group)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliographic survey only: Hervás/Díaz Taño grammar notice, Lozano's remark that Guayaná 'tenía las letras F, J y H' and admitted 'muda con líquida', apócope/síncopa; Lista 1883 and Ambrosetti vocabularies; classification with Kaingang-Ingain. Nothing on accent/stress or tone.

sources.citation: Bertoni, Moisés S. 1920. Aperçu ethnographique préliminaire du Paraguay Oriental & Haut Paraná, égard aux autres régions guaraníes. Anales Científicos Paraguayos, serie II, no. 6 (Puerto Bertoni: Ex Sylvis), sections 'Les Kimdá', 'Les Ihvihtihrokái', 'Les Ingái', 'Les Pirapihtanguá ou Guayanás modernes du Paraná', 'Les Tái', printed pp. 504–509; also his review of B. T. Martínez 1919 on p. 568.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonology. Linguistic content is limited to: the Kimdá language 'était différente' from Kaingang; 'Le glossaire que j'ai pu réunir [of the Ihvihtihrokái], accuse le 20 %, à peu près, de mots kaingangs et une proportion moindre d'éléments guaranís, mais presque le 40 % des mots se retrouve dans l'ensemble des langues krenn' (p. 506) — the glossary itself is not printed (an unpublished Bertoni manuscript, possibly in the Bertoni archive, Asunción); the Ingái 'ne parlent plus leur dialecte'; the Pirapihtanguá 'ne parlent que le guaraní.. avec la phonétique mbihá. Les vieux se rappellent encor…

sources.citation: Freitas, Affonso A. de. 1910. Os Guayanás de Piratininga. São Paulo: Laemmert. Comparative 'Vocabulario comparado' with a 'Guayaná do Paraná' column (Patiño via Ihering 1904).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonetic commentary on the Paraná Guayaná forms (searched accent/acento/pronunci/tonic/oxyt/syllab and read the source note); wordlist-only.

sources.citation: Borba, Telêmaco. 1908. Actualidade Indígena (Paraná, Brazil). Curitiba: Impressora Paranaense. pp. 136–139: remarks on Ambrosetti's Ingain and 'Vocabulário dos idiomas Guaianá e Kaingangue' (Patiño's Guaianá list with Kaingang equivalents).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonetic commentary on Guaianá/Kimdá; the list is reprinted to show the 'radical differença' from Kaingang. Wordlist-only data.

sources.citation: Martínez, Benigno T. 1904 [dated 1905 in print]. Os Indios Guayanãs. Revista do Museu Paulista 6: 45–52 (with 'Grupo Guayanã' comparative table Portuguez–Guayanã–Ingaim and Patiño's 'Vocabulario da lingua Guayanã', pp. 50–52).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonetic commentary on the Guayaná (Kimdá) language; the text quotes Azara and Lista on the people (Lista's 'voz que é aspera e dissonante' refers to their speech generally) and gives the comparative wordlists. Wordlist-only data.

sources.citation: Lista, Ramón. 1883. El Territorio de las Misiones. Buenos Aires: Imprenta 'La Universidad'. 124 pp. Appendix: 'Vocabulario de la lengua Guayaná' (Lista's own 11 items plus Patiño's 1863 list).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
